components.gap: (1) Barwise ch. A.1, 5.4, printed p.44: "To get a Completeness Theorem, for countable theories T of L_omega1omega, one must add an infinitary rule of proof." Only the necessity half is supplied (thm:p02-w02c-p02-003-infinitary-rule, owned body 880-892, owned annex 1025-1043: no sound finitary relation is complete). The positive half the source claims -- that with an infinitary rule added there is a Completeness Theorem for countable theories of L_omega1omega -- has no host with exact hypotheses and complete proof route on the Barwise route and no specific missing-work record: the only handbook statement is thm:p02-karp-completeness (variants.tex 400-405), cited=Karp1964, and neither def:p02-w02c-p02-003-beyond-boundary nor any other record names it. Supply that completeness theorem (a stated infinitary calculus, its exact hypotheses, a complete written proof) in the owned body and annex, or a specific missing-work record for it. (2) Barwise ch. A.1, after 4.9, printed p.37: "our proof used only the derived rules 4.11 (iii), (iv) so we could have used them in place of the more standard rules of H." The claim is only reported (w02-p02-005 body 1131-1134), while the same passage records that the handbook proof of 4.9 needs an added clause (v); no host states and proves which system with derived rules in place of the generalization rules is complete (with or without clause (v)), and there is no specific missing-work record. Supply that result with exact hypotheses and a complete proof, or a specific missing-work record.
